```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Read this page if you have code written for readgpt, the package's name up to
version 0.6.0, or for its first version (v1). `NEWS.md` lists every change
release by release.

## From readgpt to harnessr

harnessr was called readgpt up to version 0.6.0, and so was its GitHub
repository. The rename leaves requests, cache keys and recordings unchanged,
and caches and recordings made under the old name still answer. The old
function and option names are removed; `NEWS.md` lists each one with its
replacement.

## From v1

The v1 entry points are removed. Each one has a replacement:

| v1 | now |
|---|---|
| `answer_question(f, q, mode = "Chunked")` | `answer_document(f, q, "thorough")` |
| `parse_text(f, chunk_method = "semantic")` | `gr_ingest(f)`, then `gr_segment(doc, "semantic")` |
| `gpt_read_chunked()` | `gr_read(ch, q, cl, "map_reduce")` |
| `gpt_read_retrieval()` | `gr_read(ch, q, cl, "skim")` |
| `gpt_read_hierarchical()` | `gr_read(ch, q, cl, "hierarchical")` |
| `gpt_read_multipass()` | `gr_read(ch, q, cl, "ensemble")` |
| `readgpt_example()` | `gr_example()` |
| `options(readgpt.api_key =)` | `options(harnessr.api_key =)` |
| `options(readgpt.allow_local_urls =)` | `options(harnessr.allow_local_urls =)` |

Three behaviour changes from v1 are deliberate and will alter your results:

1. **`mode` no longer defaults to all five modes.** `answer_question(f, q)` in v1
   ran every mode: 41 API calls on an 8-paragraph document, where one was
   expected.
2. **Modes no longer contaminate each other.** In v1, `mode = c("Chunked",
   "Semantic")` changed Chunked's chunking, its cost, and its answer relative to
   `mode = "Chunked"` alone.
3. **Digits are no longer stripped by default.** v1's `remove_numbers = TRUE`
   default was unreachable from `answer_question()`, so every figure, date and
   percentage was deleted before the model saw the document.

For v1's `refine = TRUE`, ask for citations with `cite = TRUE` in
`gr_read_spec()`. Its verification pass has no replacement because it could
not run: it called a `search_text()` function that the repository never
defined.

The v1 source is kept under `legacy/` in the repository for reference and A/B
comparison. The package does not load it. To reproduce its ingestion and
chunking under the current code, use the `legacy` recipe. It strips digits, as
v1 did, and cuts 3000-token paragraph chunks with no overlap:

```{r message = FALSE}
library(harnessr)
old <- hr_options(verbose = FALSE)
legacy <- gr_recipes("legacy")
gr_ingest("Revenue was 45.2 million dollars in fiscal 2024.", legacy$ingest)$text
unlist(legacy$segment[c("method", "max_tokens", "overlap_tokens")])
```

```{r include = FALSE}
hr_options(old)
```

The regression suite in `tests/testthat/` reproduces each of these defects
against the current code.
